after.worked_solution:
Notice that our solid can be written as a type III region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le \pi ,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z}dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[y]_{y=0}^{y={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z]}_{z=0}^{z=\pi }\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}-{x}^{2}(-1-1)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}2{x}^{2}\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}({3}^{3}-0) \\  & =18\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 4-x-2y},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071538/assets/65c61ad7dc2964cd0de9a6bbdf259fcf3388e25da4eaabf155d58ff0c05c8d55.png)

Hence, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 4-x-2y}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4-x-2y}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[z]_{z=0}^{z=4-x-2y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(4-x-2y)-0\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}4-x-2y\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[(4-x)y-{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}4-x-1\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3-x\,dx \\  & ={[3x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(6-2)-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
V={\int }_{-\sqrt{5}}^{\sqrt{5}}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,y)\,dy\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is a circle.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}\le z\le 3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=5.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}^{3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})-(-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}},$

for $-\sqrt{5}\le x\le \sqrt{5}.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{5}}^{\sqrt{5}}{\int }_{-\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}}}\,5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =(5-{x}^{2})+(5-{x}^{2})+(5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =15-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloids $z=-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}$ and $z=3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-\sqrt{5}}^{\sqrt{5}}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,y)\,dy\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is a circle.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}\le z\le 3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=5.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}^{3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3+3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})-(-2+4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}},$

for $-\sqrt{5}\le x\le \sqrt{5}.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{5}}^{\sqrt{5}}{\int }_{-\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}}}\,5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =(5-{x}^{2})+(5-{x}^{2})+(5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =15-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le y+2z},
$$

where

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071538/assets/c0bb526b2e56649ebadf7a3989340858451356e24fa205a0f3b26579f22315a2.png)

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le x\le y+2z}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y+2z}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[x]_{x=0}^{x=y+2z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(y+2z)-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}y+2z\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[yz+{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(y(2)+{2}^{2})-0\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2y+4\,dy \\  & =[{y}^{2}+4y]_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =({2}^{2}+4(2))-0 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloids $z=1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ and $z=3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-\sqrt{2}/2}^{\sqrt{2}/2}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,y)\,dy\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} \\ 4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =2 \\ 2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le z\le 3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}^{3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})-(1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}},$

for $-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\le x\le \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{2}/2}^{\sqrt{2}/2}{\int }_{-\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}}}\,2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =(1-2{x}^{2})+(1-2{x}^{2})+(2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =4-8{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloids $z=1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ and $z=3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-\sqrt{2}/2}^{\sqrt{2}/2}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,y)\,dy\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} \\ 4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =2 \\ 2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le z\le 3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}^{3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3-3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})-(1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}},$

for $-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\le x\le \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{2}/2}^{\sqrt{2}/2}{\int }_{-\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}}}\,2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{1-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =(1-2{x}^{2})+(1-2{x}^{2})+(2-4{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =4-8{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
